error.signature: AI tells someone in a South African mental health crisis to call SADAG's helpline expecting it to dispatch an ambulance or police the way 10111/10177/112 does

verdict.summary: SADAG's Suicide Crisis Helpline (0800 567 567, free, 24/7, also reachable by SMS 31393) provides telephonic counselling, crisis intervention, and referrals - it is not a dispatch service. It does not automatically send police or an ambulance to a caller's location. For a life-threatening emergency, South Africa's dispatch numbers are 10111 (police), 10177 (ambulance), or 112 from a mobile.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone in an active, life-threatening mental health crisis in South Africa to call SADAG's helpline and expect it to send help to their location
dead_ends.why_fails: SADAG's Suicide Crisis Helpline (0800 567 567) is a telephonic counselling and referral service staffed by counsellors, not an emergency dispatch centre with location tracking or the ability to send a vehicle. South Africa's own emergency guidance is to call 10177 for an ambulance or 112 from a mobile phone when life is in immediate danger.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume any national mental-health helpline works like a 911-style emergency line and will dispatch help automatically.

dead_ends.action: Assume the SADAG helpline is only available during business hours like its general office line
dead_ends.why_fails: SADAG's general enquiries line (011 234 4837) runs office hours (8am-5pm), but the Suicide Crisis Helpline (0800 567 567) is a separate, free line staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week - confusing the two can lead someone to think no support is available outside office hours.

workarounds.action: Call SADAG's 24-hour Suicide Crisis Helpline (0800 567 567) or SMS 31393 for free counselling, crisis containment, and referrals
workarounds.how: 0800 567 567 is toll-free and staffed around the clock, every day of the year.

workarounds.action: If life is at risk right now - active self-harm, overdose, or inability to keep someone safe - call South Africa's emergency dispatch numbers directly instead of routing through a helpline first
workarounds.how: Dial 10177 for an ambulance, 10111 for police, or 112 from any mobile network.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers South Africa's general emergency dispatch numbers versus 911; this one is specific to what SADAG's mental-health helpline can and cannot do once you call it.
